Fluxus describes its field as visual arts in the broadest sense across all disciplines, and the curatorial criteria name contemporary art, so a photography curator is in scope; the fund says it will prioritise innovative practices and the production of new works. The call page names no application fee at any point. Applications go through a Google Form and must be written in English, and the fund asks you to send a confirmation email to its own address as well as submitting the form. Fluxus Art Projects is a Franco-British fund supported by the Institut français du Royaume-Uni, the British Council, Arts Council England, Creative Scotland and the French Ministry of Culture; it also runs the Magnetic artist residencies in tandem pairs of a French region with a UK nation, and prizes at Frieze London and Art Basel Paris, all of which are closed at the time of writing. Applications are selected by the fund's standing Artistic Committee, named on its About page: Hélène Nguyen-Ban as chair, Margot Heller of the South London Gallery, Caroline Bourgeois of the Bourse du Commerce, Wells Fray-Smith of the Barbican, Daria de Beauvais of the Palais de Tokyo, Martin Clark of Camden Art Centre, Nicolas Gausserand of the musées d'Orsay and the Orangerie, and Edward Gillman of Chisenhale Gallery, alongside representatives of the public partners. The fund publishes no notification date for this round. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 research grant.

item.title: Premier Prix photographique du Musée Postal
item.description: The first photography prize created by the Musée Postal in Paris — the museum of La Poste, founded in 1946, a Musée de France and a corporate museum holding a photographic collection of some 250,000 documents — launched for the Bicentenary of Photography. It funds the production of one new photographic project on La Poste today, with a grant of €15,000 (TTC) paid directly to the artist. The brief is open as to approach and tight as to subject: the project must look at the contemporary postal world in its human, material and/or immaterial dimensions, must continue the applicant's existing artistic practice, and must offer an original, contemporary view. The museum names mobility and flows, ecological transformation, technological innovation, territorial presence, and trades and social questions as examples of what a project might address, and states that every photographic approach is welcome — documentary, reportage, fine-art and experimental alike. Applications are open only to professional photographers, with no age limit, resident in France (metropolitan or overseas) and able to prove professional status: an URSSAF attestation, artiste-auteur status, a Kbis extract or a production-company attestation are all accepted as proof. There is no entry fee. The dossier goes by email as a PDF attachment of no more than 10 MB — the règlement recommends, but does not require, that it be a single file — and must contain an illustrated artistic portfolio of at most six pages covering the applicant's practice and earlier work, a statement of intent of at most two pages with a 500-character summary, a CV or account of the applicant's path with full contact details and a copy of a valid ID, and the proof of professional status; anything illegible, incomplete or late is ruled inadmissible without being read. Selection runs in two stages — the jury reads every dossier and preselects a number of applicants by 15 December 2026, then those applicants present their project to the jury in person at the museum (or remotely if necessary) on 6 January 2027, after which the winner is chosen and told by email, and possibly by telephone, at the end of the deliberation. The jury is named in full and is substantial: it includes the director of the agency Signatures, the museum's own director, a professor of art history at the Beaux-arts de Paris, the cultural lead at Magnum Photos, and an artist teaching at the ENSP in Arles. Beyond the money, a selection of signed and numbered prints from the winning project enters the museum's collection — their production is paid for and carried out by La Fabrique de l'image, the prize's partner laboratory in Meysse, Ardèche — and the winner gets privileged access and support within the La Poste group to make the work. Two conditions are worth reading before applying: the règlement requires the applicant to state explicitly in the project description and/or statement of intent whether any image or video is generated or transformed with an AI tool, naming the tools and the extent of their use, with failure to disclose grounds for disqualification even after the winner has been named; and payment of the grant is conditional on signing a copyright assignment contract with the museum covering the works produced, which sets out the rights assigned, their duration and territory, and a non-exclusive assignment of reproduction and representation rights. The museum reserves the right not to award the prize if it judges the dossiers insufficient, and may adjust the calendar, announcing any change on its own website. Production of the series runs February–June 2027 and the prints are made in July 2027. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €15,000 production grant.

item.title: Expressions West 2027 · Coos Art Museum
item.description: The 2027 edition of Coos Art Museum's annual regional juried exhibition, open to artists living in thirteen western states — Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. Coos Art Museum is the only art museum on the Oregon Coast, housed in Coos Bay's 1936 Art Deco former post office, and Expressions West is its survey of what is being made across the American West — no theme, work judged on its own terms. Photography is an explicitly eligible medium alongside painting, drawing, hand-pulled prints, mixed media, fiber and textiles, small sculpture, glass, turned and carved wood, jewellery and furniture; prints must be framed and ready for hanging and no work may exceed 48 inches in any direction including the frame. Read the exclusions before you pay: digital artwork, AI artwork, video, film, audio and giclée prints are all ineligible, so an inkjet-printed photograph does not qualify and the call wants a photographic print made another way. The juror for 2027 is Daemian Hawthorn, an artist working across drawing, painting and welded metal sculpture. Awards are $1,000 for First Place, $750 for Second and $250 for Third. Up to three works may be submitted, with five images allowed per artwork; the fee is $35 for the first submission and $10 each for the second and third. The museum states the schedule in full: submissions close 9 December 2026, acceptance or rejection is notified on 22 December 2026, accepted artwork must reach the museum by 23 January 2027, the opening reception is 6 February 2027, and work is retrieved in person on 23–24 April 2027 or returned by courier on 24 April. Artwork is insured from arrival until return. Artists are responsible for getting work back: you may arrange and pay for your own return shipping, or ask the museum to coordinate it and be charged the shipping costs plus a $30 handling fee. Work made under an instructor's supervision is not eligible, and entries must be original in concept, composition and execution. Work must have been made in the last two years (2024–2026), must not have been shown at Coos Art Museum before, and if it is part of a series the entered piece has to be distinguishable from your others. Sales are the artist's own: the museum takes no commission and processes no transactions, so you set the price and deal with the buyer directly. The date that was in conflict has resolved: as of 31 October 2026 the record's own Important Dates block and its machine deadline field agree on 9 December 2026 (23:59:59 Pacific), and the 6 December an earlier reading found appears nowhere on the record. — Deadline: December 9, 2026. Fee: $35 first work + $10 each additional (up to 3). Prize: $1,000 / $750 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: Being Seen 2027 · TAG/The Artists Gallery
item.description: A regional juried exhibition at TAG/The Artists Gallery, an artist-run gallery at 501 N Market Street in Frederick, Maryland, hung in the gallery itself from 5 to 28 March 2027 with a reception on 6 March, 5–8 pm. The gallery's premise for the show: "If a tree falls in a forest, does it make a sound? It does only if there is an observer. Art also needs an observer to truly Be Seen because art is not complete until it connects with the heart and mind of the viewer." The juror is Florencio Lennox (Lenny) Campello — an artist, curator, critic and author of 100 Artists of Washington, DC, who has juried or curated over 200 fine art shows and recently assembled the Women Artists of the DMV survey across twenty venues in the capital region. Photographs in both analog and digital formats are explicitly eligible, alongside original paintings, drawings, prints, mixed media including digital collage and manipulations, and sculpture; work must have been made in the last three years, must not have been shown at TAG before, and no reproductions of pre-existing artwork or video are accepted. Awards, chosen by the juror, are $500 First Prize, $250 Second, $125 Third and three Honorable Mentions of $50 each. The eligibility bar is tight and worth reading twice: open to artists 18 and over living in Maryland, DC, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania or Delaware, within easy driving distance of Frederick, and not currently represented by TAG. That driving-distance clause is enforced by the logistics rather than by a map — there is no shipping option in either direction, and accepted work must be hand-delivered to the gallery on 28 February or 1 March 2027 (2–6 pm) and collected on 28 or 29 March, with $5 a day charged for storage after that and disposal possible after thirty days. All wall-hung work including the frame must stay within 48 inches in any direction and 6 inches deep, under 30 lbs, framed and ready to hang with wire or a cleat — no sawtooth hangers. All work must be for sale with no price-on-request, and the gallery takes 30% commission. Judging runs 13–24 January 2027 and the gallery aims to notify every applicant by 29 January. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: $35 first work + $5 each additional (up to 3). Prize: $500 / $250 / $125 + three $50 honorable mentions + Exhibition.

item.title: Dream of Home Away · Van Der Plas Gallery
item.description: The next cycle of Van Der Plas Gallery's year-round Open Call Program, for a group exhibition titled Dream of Home Away at the gallery's Lower East Side space at 156 Orchard Street, on view 12–25 February 2027 with an opening reception on 12 February, 6–8 pm. Founded in New York City in the 1980s, the gallery shows emerging and established contemporary artists with a focus on downtown culture, outsider art, street art, painting, sculpture and experimental practices, and photography is named explicitly among the media it wants — alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media, digital art and experimental practices. The brief is not thematic in any strict sense: the gallery says it looks for "originality, conceptual clarity, and a strong artistic vision" and work that reflects the diversity of contemporary practice, and the exhibition is meant to bring together different practices from artists at different career stages inside a professional gallery setting. Applying is open to artists at any stage, internationally, with no age or residence bar: $35 buys the review of up to four artworks (JPG), plus installation images for any framed or otherwise applicable work, an artist bio and an artist statement of 100–200 words each. Submissions are read on a rolling basis by the gallery's own curatorial team, selection is not guaranteed, and work submitted now is considered for Dream of Home Away first and then stays under consideration for later exhibitions in the programme; artists may apply again at any time and each submission is read independently. Selected artists are contacted directly by email, with no published notification date. The commercial terms are worth knowing before you pay: the gallery states the $35 covers submission review, administrative coordination, exhibition planning and the running costs of a physical gallery; all shipping, delivery and return arrangements and their costs fall on the artist, including for international applicants; every accepted work must be available for sale for the run of the show, with pricing agreed with the gallery after acceptance, and work not for sale may be declined or excluded; and the framing specification is enforced — work on paper must be framed, with a recommended minimum two-inch mat, a museum-style frame in natural wood, black or whitewashed finish and plexiglass rather than glass, and work that does not meet it "may be excluded from the exhibition, even after delivery". The gallery will frame to spec for an additional fee on request. The binding document is a Terms and Conditions PDF linked from the call page, last updated 25 October 2026, and it carries five things the page itself does not: sales made during or as a result of the exhibition are split 50% artist / 50% gallery; submitted work must not exceed 48 by 60 inches, and anything over 36 by 48 inches has to be shipped unstretched; artists must supply a prepaid return shipping label and email a copy to the gallery; unsold work left past the collection date incurs a $250 storage fee after three days and may be donated or discarded after a month, with no compensation; and every applicant, selected or not, is told the outcome in the first week of January. The same document sets no age, residence or AI condition. — Deadline: January 22, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: PHODAR Biennial 14 — Traces Remain · PHODAR Foundation
item.description: The 14th edition of the PHODAR Biennial, Bulgaria's oldest international photography competition — running since 1999 and organised by the PHODAR Foundation in Sofia, with the Sofia Municipality Culture Programme and exhibitions historically staged at the National Gallery — asks for a coherent series on the theme "Traces Remain". The title is borrowed from the novel by the Bulgarian writer Pavel Vezhinov, and the brief runs through Susan Sontag's On Photography: the photograph as a trace of reality, physically connected to what once stood before the lens, and at the same time a reminder of transience. The organisers' questions are the interesting part — "How do we read the traces of the past in the present? What do abandoned spaces, altered landscapes, family archives and marks on the human body reveal? Which traces do we deliberately preserve, and which do we try to erase? Can a photograph sustain a memory when its story has already been lost?" — and they say the theme is open to any genre that answers them, documentary, portraiture or conceptual alike, including work on social conflict, generational relationships and the transformation of surroundings. Entry is free and there are two sections, each author choosing one: the Grand Prize section and Debut, the latter reserved for authors at the beginning of a career without serious national or international achievements yet. A separate Award for Humanistic Photography goes to one author regardless of section. Submissions are a series or photo essay of 8 to 20 images from an ongoing or completed project, JPEG, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side at 300 DPI, numbered in the order you want them read; the work has to have been made on or after 1 January 2025, with an exception for long-term projects begun earlier and continued since. Stock photography is not accepted, one series per author, and collaborative series by two or more photographers are explicitly welcome. Entry is open to professional and amateur photographers over 18 with no restriction on country of origin or citizenship. Finalists' prints are produced and mounted at the Foundation's expense for the PHODAR Awards exhibition in Sofia, the prints staying with the Foundation; copyright remains with the photographer throughout, and selected authors are shown in an online winners gallery and published in the edition photobook. Past award winners the Foundation names include Donald Weber (VII Photo Agency) and Mila Teshaieva. Note one disagreement between the organiser's own surfaces: the rules page states a deadline of 1 January 2027 while the submission form at entry.phodar.net prints "DEADLINE IS 31.12.2026" — the earlier, form-stated date is the one to work to, and the rules add that the Foundation may extend without notice. Prizes are paid in euros once the Foundation has received the award funding, with any international payment or conversion charges deducted from the prize. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €2,000 Grand Prize + €600 Debut Award + €600 Humanistic Photography Award + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Visual Art Open Prize 2027
item.description: The 12th edition of the Visual Art Open, a UK-based international art award with a £10,000 prize fund and a dedicated Photography & Digital Art category alongside Painting, Sculpture, Drawing & Illustration, Mixed Media/Collage/Printmaking, Student Artist and Art Educator. The overall winner takes £2,000 in cash, a solo exhibition at a London venue, a place in the London finalists' show at the Minster Building, a dedicated article on their practice, and a year of Visual Artists Association premium membership with its mentorship and Momentum business-development programmes. Each category winner receives £250, the same VAA membership and course, a place in the finalists' exhibition, an article and extra online promotion. All finalists are invited to exhibit in central London and receive a certificate; every entrant is put forward for promotion across the VAA's social channels and its 60,000-subscriber mailing list. Entry is open worldwide to artists at every career stage, from first-time entrants to established practitioners, and the organisers make a point of discounted rates for students and art educators, which stay fixed across the whole entry period. Work is submitted as JPEG or PNG images up to 5MB, up to five per entry, and the number of works has to be chosen before checkout because the price changes with it. Judging is by a panel drawn from commercial galleries, museums, art media and academia — recent panels have included the creative director of Mall Galleries, the senior fair manager of The Other Art Fair, and the critic Tabish Khan — though the organisers have not yet published the panel under the 2027 label. The prize is funded by entry fees, donations, art sales, advertising and sponsorship rather than by Arts Council money, and entries cannot be refunded once submitted. Early-bird pricing runs to 17 December 2026; standard pricing applies from 18 December 2026 until the entry period closes on 25 March 2027. The terms page adds bars and costs the entry pages never mention: entry is open from age 14, with written authorisation from a legal guardian for anyone under 18; work must have been made within the last three years and must not already have been sold; and a 40% commission is taken on anything that sells through the VAO exhibition. AI work is barred outright — the rules require that every submission be “created manually and entirely by the artist”, and state that “AI-generated or AI-assisted artwork is not eligible for entry”. One number is worth doing yourself: of the advertised £10,000 fund the published cash is £3,750 — £2,000 to the overall winner and £250 to each of the seven category winners — with the balance made up of the VAA memberships, courses, London exhibition places and certificates listed above. — Deadline: March 25, 2027. Fee: £15–£55 early bird (1–5 works), £20–£60 from 18 Dec; £10–£35 student/educator. Prize: £10,000 fund — £2,000 + solo exhibition in London.

item.title: Amsterdam Artist Showcase — February 2027 · Arrival Gallery
item.description: Arrival Gallery's three-day group showcase in Amsterdam, 12 to 14 February 2027, at Zesde Vogelstraat 40 in the city's west. The gallery takes submissions from painters, photographers, sculptors, illustrators, textile, mixed-media and digital artists, and describes itself as working with emerging, independent and mid-career practitioners. Photographic, moving-image and screen-based work is explicitly catered for: alongside hung physical work, Arrival presents digital pieces through curated display screens, digital exhibition formats, online artist features and city activations, which makes the digital route a realistic option for a photographer who does not want to ship and frame prints. Submitting work for review is free and there is no entry fee. The cost comes after selection, and Arrival publishes the floors rather than hiding them: the Digital Showcase route starts from £65 and the Physical Showcase route from £165, with the full format, timeline and preparation details sent to selected artists before they confirm a place. Applicants pick their preferred route — digital, physical or featured — when they submit, or ask the gallery to recommend one. Places are sold from a limited release, so the gallery's own framing is that confirmation secures a slot from the current batch rather than that selection alone guarantees a wall. Anyone considering this should read it for what it is: a paid-participation showcase, free to enter, where the real decision comes once a price is quoted. — Deadline: January 28, 2027. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: København Noir — Din By i Sort-Hvid · Copenhagen Photo Festival
item.description: A free black-and-white photo hunt through Copenhagen's old working-class districts, run by Copenhagen Photo Festival with Københavns Museum, CEWE and a group of Copenhagen photographers under the city's Vinter i København programme. Nine archive photographs from the museum's collection have been installed outdoors on the streets and squares of Nørrebro, Vesterbro and Nordvest — each one at the spot where it was originally taken. The task is to find them, one or two or all nine, and submit your own black-and-white pictures made in the area around them. The festival's framing is unapologetically atmospheric: a tribute to contrast, to the aesthetics of decay and renewal, to street life and dusk, to "that Copenhagen which is rarely captured", and to the time of year Danes associate with endless darkness — the page opens with Henrik Nordbrandt's line that the year has sixteen months, "November, December, January... November, November, November, November". Street photography in black and white is what the organisers say they are after, worked alone or with others. Entry is free and every submitted photograph is automatically in the running to be exhibited at Absalon on 22 November, the day the project culminates at the festival's off-season photo market. Three guided photo walks with the photographers Christopher 'Flip' Egeberg, Jón Bjarni Hjartarson and Christine Lorenzen run alongside the hunt, offering black-and-white street technique to anyone who wants it. The entry terms, which live on the CEWE contest platform rather than on the festival's own page, restrict entry to people resident in Copenhagen ("Deltagelsesberettigede er fysiske personer, som har bopæl i København"), and the work has to be made around the nine specific locations, so this is for people who live in the city and are in it before 3 November; entrants under 18 confirm that a parent or guardian has read the terms and consents. The same terms set out what is actually awarded: the contest runs in nine categories, one per location, with a maximum of one photograph per category; a specialist jury picks 27 winning images (three per location) for the Absalon show and ranks the best three, where first prize is CEWE photo products worth DKK 2,000, second is Christopher 'Flip' Egeberg's photobook about the street artist SPYO, given by Københavns Museum, and third is a voucher for two tickets to Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027. Winners are told by email, with no notification date published, and nothing is posted out — prizes are handed over at Absalon on 22 November or collected afterwards from the festival office. Images made wholly by computer or by artificial intelligence are barred and will be excluded, retouching that adds or removes content is not allowed, and the extent of any editing has to be stated in the image description. The festival calls it a taste of next year's edition, when the hunt returns at larger scale as Copenhagen Photo Festival moves from June to November. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: DKK 2,000 in CEWE products + Exhibition at Absalon, 22 November.

item.title: 1839 Awards Art of Photography Contest
item.description: The 2026 edition of the 1839 Awards' Art of Photography Contest, which the organiser frames as celebrating "the creativity, vision, and distinctive perspectives that make photography an art form, across every genre". It takes over from the Art of Storytelling Contest, whose own page is still up but carries the finished 2025 edition (8 September 2025 to 14 January 2026); the site now lists three annual contests: Photographer of the Year, Art of Photography and Color Photography. MIND THE TWO DEADLINES. The contest page's headline reads "Deadline: November 18", but its own submissions-due panel sets out three stages: early bird 26 October only, regular entry 26 October to 18 November, and an extended entry deadline running 18 November to 18 December. Entries are therefore still accepted until 18 December, which is the date carried here — but the prices below are the regular-stage ones, and the contest's own pricing record discounts the regular stage while leaving the extended stage undiscounted, so expect to pay more after 18 November. Pay-per-entry pricing runs in three tiers — $15 student / $25 non-pro / $30 pro for a single image, and $30 / $40 / $50 for a series on the same tiers — with credit bundles at $88 / $105 for five and $175 / $210 for ten, which the organiser advertises as up to 30% cheaper than paying per entry. A professional is defined as someone who sells or publishes regularly or has earned the majority of their income from photography; everyone else may enter as a non-professional. There is also a rolling fee-waiver route: 1839 runs a scholarship programme for applicants from communities underserved or underrepresented in the creative world, applied for by email with a short statement naming the contest. Awards are cash and the figures are published: $1,500, $749 and $250 for the three professional places and $900, $400 and $200 for the three non-professional ones, $3,999 in all, which this contest's page rounds up to "$4,000+ in cash prizes". The eighteen category placings (gold, silver and bronze in each) carry a trophy and a certificate but no cash. There is also international media coverage, a profile in the 1839 Artist Directory, a published interview in 1839 Magazine, and press releases, badges and certificates for awarded work. Judging is blind and two-stage, with a nominated shortlist per category and aggregated judge rankings deciding the winners; the three judges shown on this contest's page are drawn from a wider 1839 panel of nineteen that includes staff from the Whitney Museum, Phillips, Christie's, Getty Images, the Centre Pompidou, Bonhams, Serpentine, Vanity Fair and the New York Times. Entry is open worldwide to anyone eighteen or over, excluding staff and family of parent company Creative Resource Collective, LLC and of the jury. Previously published, exhibited or awarded images are welcome, there is no requirement that the work be recent, and exclusivity is not required. Files must be JPEG or PNG, at least 1500 pixels on the longest edge and under 10MB, unwatermarked; film, digital and phone captures are all accepted in any orientation. You keep all rights — "we do not become the owner of your work when you submit an entry", no copyright or moral rights are claimed and entries are not sold on, though 1839 may use submissions to promote the competition with credit. ON AI THE ORGANISER CONTRADICTS ITSELF, AND FOR THIS CONTEST THE ANSWER IS NO. Its central rules page says, twice, that "AI-generated images are only admissible in a designated category as specified in any 1839 Awards contest", while this contest page's own entry-eligibility panel carries the flatter line that "AI-generated images are not admissible in any 1839 Awards contest". The contest's own category list settles which of the two applies here: eighteen categories, from Abstract and Documentary to Street & Urban Life and Wildlife, and not one of them is an AI category, so there is nowhere in this call for an AI-generated image to be admitted. 1839 also reserves the right to demand proof that an image was not AI-generated. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $15 / $25 / $30 single, $30 / $40 / $50 series. Prize: $1,500 1st prize + 1839 Magazine interview.

item.title: Portrait of Britain Vol. 9 · 1854 Media
item.description: The ninth volume of Portrait of Britain, the annual award run by 1854 Media, publisher of the British Journal of Photography, and billed by the organiser as "the UK's biggest annual photography exhibition". Winning portraits are shown up and down the country for a month on JCDecaux UK digital screens, and winners also get a chance to be featured in the British Journal of Photography and have their work sent to 1854's national and international press list — past volumes have been picked up by the Guardian, the Independent, the BBC, Sky News, Aesthetica and It's Nice That. The archive on 1854's own site shows the recent pattern: a shortlist of 200 photographs, from which 100 winning images are drawn. There is no cash prize. The Vol. 9 jury is Vanley Burke, Adama Jalloh, Ingrid Pollard, Mimi Mollica and Kalpesh Lathigra (photographers), Anna Liesching (art curator, National Museums NI), Dr Ajamu X (artist and archive curator), Francis Hodgson (founder, Prix Pictet), Tom Booth Woodger (publisher, Bluecoat Press) and Mick Moore, Zoe Harrison and Sinead Solomon of the British Journal of Photography. The award is open to professional and non-professional photographers of all ages and to international as well as UK-based entrants, but the restriction is on the picture, not the photographer: the image itself must have been shot in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland) after 1 January 2025, and may be of an individual or a group. Entries are single images, JPEG only, up to 10MB each, with a title under 200 characters and a description under 2,000 characters. Written consent from the subject (or a parent or guardian for a minor) is required to appear in the outdoor exhibition; verbal permission is enough for the shortlist. Entry is priced per image slot — £10 for one, £20 for three, £35 for ten, £60 for twenty — and 1854 Access Members (Full or Digital) can submit ten images free as part of their membership, though they must stay members through judging and the exhibition for their entries to remain eligible. Fees are non-refundable. The cutoff is not end of day in every zone: the terms state "The deadline for entries is 5th November 2026 – 23:59 (UK Time)". No copyright is transferred, but entrants grant 1854 and JCDecaux the right to display and publish entries without payment for the purposes of the award and its publicity. On AI the terms are explicit: "We accept entries that consist of original photographs modified by AI. However, all significant AI modifications must be clearly indicated in the caption." — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: £10 / £20 / £35 / £60 (1 / 3 / 10 / 20 images). Prize: UK-wide JCDecaux screen exhibition.

item.title: Project Nexus Supported Residencies 2027 — Nigerian Diaspora Visual Artist · Guest Artists Space (G.A.S.) Foundation
item.description: The third residency in the 2027 round of Project Nexus, run by the Guest Artists Space (G.A.S.) Foundation and the Yinka Shonibare Foundation with the support of Deutsche Bank — a four-week residency at G.A.S. Lagos, 8 March – 2 April 2027, for an artist of the global Nigerian Diaspora. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture, film, installation, ceramics, textiles, printmaking and performance. The residency offers time to develop existing research, build relationships with artists, practitioners and cultural networks in Nigeria, and explore new connections with Nigerian contexts, histories and material practices; there is no requirement to produce a finished work. This one is part-funded and the organiser is explicit about the gap: a ₦2,660,000 residency award towards food, living expenses and materials, a private en-suite bedroom, studio and shared workspace, library access, on-site support and the G.A.S. driver are provided, but international travel, visa costs, insurance and personal or project-related expenses are NOT included, and applicants are encouraged to seek additional mobility or project funding from arts councils, foundations, cultural agencies or universities. Trips outside Lagos and Ijebu are also at the resident's own cost. Applicants must be Nigerian nationals or of Nigerian heritage living and working outside Nigeria, aged 23 or over at any career stage with an established body of work, available for the fixed dates, proficient in spoken and written English, and able to name a referee from a curator, gallerist or cultural institution familiar with their work. The application asks for a single PDF portfolio with research examples, a CV, a short biography (150 words), referee contact details and six written answers of 150 or 200 words — five required, plus an optional one on practice and research — which may be given as a video statement instead. Applications close at midnight WAT on 3 November 2026 and no fee is charged; a selection panel is announced in November 2026 and final selections on 7 December 2026. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: ₦2,660,000 stipend + accommodation & studio in Lagos.
